reviews.title: Used service for 4 months zero interviews in that time span.
reviews.text:
I used Sprout for four months, and unfortunately, I cannot recommend the service based on my experience.

Over those four months, I received nothing but rejections, while several opportunities were eventually closed by the client. I understand that no job platform can guarantee employment, but after paying for the service for four months, I expected to see at least some meaningful results or opportunities that progressed beyond rejection.

What made the experience even more frustrating was the customer service. After deciding to cancel, I emailed Sprout to ask about a refund and never received a response. Not even an acknowledgment.

Ultimately, I paid for four months of a service that produced no positive results for me, and when I reached out with a legitimate question about a refund, I was completely ignored.

Based on my experience, Sprout was not worth the money, and the lack of response from customer support left an especially poor impression.

reviews.title: Great Concept, Entirely Useless Results
reviews.text:
Sprout advertises itself as a modern, effortless job search platform that uses a simple "swipe left, swipe right" interface to match you with top employers. While the app design is sleek and swiping through listings takes zero effort, the platform is fundamentally broken where it actually counts: landing interviews.

After using Sprout for several weeks and swiping right on dozens of roles that perfectly matched my experience and qualifications, the outcome was universally dismal. Every single application resulted in an almost immediate automated rejection or a polite rejection email shortly after.

It feels less like a real recruitment tool and more like an automated rejection simulator. The AI matching algorithm seems completely disconnected from what hiring companies are actually looking for, pushing your profile into ATS resume screeners that flag and reject you instantly. Swiping right takes one second, but it yields a 100% rejection rate.

Save your time and money and stick to traditional job boards or direct company applications. Sprout makes applying effortless, but it makes getting hired impossible.

reviews.title: No pudding, no proof
reviews.text:
The idea behind this app is great but forcing me to pay before proving that it will be even remotely useful is not gonna happen. You need to prove it before I subscribe to ANYTHING. Forcing me to put in a location when I will only consider remote roles is another red flag. And making the address fields required is a huge red flag. Any job application that requires an address is a scam. Legit job applications might ask what state you intend to work from if they aren’t registered in all 50, but wouldn’t need an address until doing onboarding paperwork. So that’s very sketchy. 

Also, to potential users: the app asks for a rating during onboarding. So anyone who complied with that request gave a rating based on nothing since they hadn’t actually used the app yet. Keep that in mind if you see a bunch of positive reviews. They aren’t legitimate.

reviews.title: Misleading
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with my first experience using this app for two reasons: 

1) Leave a review prompt before using the app. The app asks you to leave a review before you’ve had any chance to explore its features or even get past the paywall. It’s hard to give an honest or accurate review without actually using the app first. Seems like they’re intentionally asking early on (before the paywall) to get more 5 starts from optimistic users early on before they get any disappointments.

2) Unexpected paywall after providing personal information. After entering full name and email address, creating an account, I hit a paywall that wasn’t at all signposted beforehand. There’s no free trial or a way to get a feel for the app before committing. Again this is intentional to be misleading onboarding process to ensure they get more downloads or something.

Both of these go against Apple’s rules about requesting a review before the user has had a chance to meaningfully experience the app. And about disclosing pricing before requiring a sign up which is also quite questionable in terms of consumer law as well. (Withholding info that would affect someone’s decision to sign up - like pricing!)

reviews.text: Sprout seemed like it would be a great way to find jobs but it’s really not worth it. You have to pay to use the app. So you’re paying to find a job. Also, not all the job listings are accurate. The listings will say it’s a remote position but going to the company’s site shows the job is actually on site. Lastly, there’s a weird email system. Sprout sends you emails from employers, and you can only contact the employer if you reply to Sprout’s email.

reviews.title: i want a refund
reviews.text: i logged in using my gmail account and I even paid and received a receipt. However, I've tried to use both the web browser and the app and neither one of them works. It just keeps looping me between the welcome to sprout page and the invite friends page. The browser situation is worse where it still takes me to the checkout page even after I've already paid when I click "get started". I tried reading online to see if anyone is facing the same issues but nobody seems to be talking about it. Maybe I'm just super unlucky or maybe this whole thing is a scam I'm not sure yet.

I don’t really understand why I have to pay to find a job…the whole point I’m looking for a job is to get payed. If it was a bit cheaper it would be more reasonable but £20 a week?! They are having a laugh

reviews.title: DO NOT DOWNLOAD
reviews.text: All the AD’s you see on social media about this app is paid acting. I downloaded the app myself looking for a job and in order to even use the app you have to pay there’s no option for free or anything. You have to pay in order to look at jobs, it gives you options for yearly payments, monthly or weekly. I automatically deleted my account, and deleted the app. There is no reason why you should haveto pay in order to look for a job.
